clue.text: Only a couple of bookies gamble — may this have restricted the figure?

definitions.text: may this have restricted the figure?

indicators.note: a couple of means the opening two letters of the word bookies are taken

parts.note: to dice is to gamble, playing at dice

explanation.surface: A punter wonders whether betting might have limited the size of the bookmakers' total.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figure' looks like a sum of money but is a woman's shape; 'a couple of' takes BO from bookies.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-fitting woman's garment that shaped and constrained the torso, hence restricting the figure.

clue.text: Verse form everyone's instructed about

indicators.note: about means the instruction word goes round the word for everyone

parts.note: bade, past of bid, means instructed or ordered
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A poetic form that everyone has been told to learn.
explanation.definitionFit: A French poetic form with three stanzas and an envoi, using a refrain.

clue.text: Agony for Dickens, almost broke when ultimate account's due

indicators.note: broke means the letters are shattered and reassembled
almost means the last letter of Dickens is dropped

explanation.surface: Charles Dickens suffered agony, nearly bankrupt when his final bill came due.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broke' looks like poverty, fitting Dickens's family history, but it signals the anagram of AGONY, FOR and DICKEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical Judgement Day, when everyone must answer for their deeds, an ultimate settling of accounts.

clue.text: Whence water's drawn back, south of Sark etc

indicators.note: in a down clue, south of means the word for back comes below

parts.note: Sark is one of the Channel Islands, abbreviated CI
the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: Where water is drawn back to the south of Sark and other islands.
explanation.walkthrough: Sark is a small island in the English Channel near Guernsey.
explanation.definitionFit: A tank or reservoir that holds stored water to be drawn off.

clue.text: Dirty look from cow at end of milking?

indicators.note: end of points to the final letter of the word milking

parts.note: a cow lows, so one that moos is a lower

explanation.surface: A cow at the end of milking time gives the farmer a resentful stare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cow' is not the animal itself but something that lows, i.e. moos.
explanation.definitionFit: A scowl or angry stare is often called a dirty look.

clue.text: Elevated trail taken regularly through country

indicators.note: in a down clue, elevated means lifted so it reads upwards
taken regularly picks alternate letters of trail

parts.note: via means through or by way of

explanation.surface: A raised path runs through the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken regularly' picks TAL from trail; 'Elevated' turns it to LAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A Baltic state, a nation bordering Estonia and Lithuania.

clue.text: Privileged American talking rubbish in exaggerated style

parts.note: WASP is White Anglo-Saxon Protestant, the privileged US elite

indicators.note: talking says the word is spoken, giving one spelt differently

parts.note: waste means rubbish

explanation.surface: A privileged American talks rubbish in an overblown way.
explanation.definitionFit: A tightly cinched, very narrow middle is an exaggerated fashion silhouette.

clue.text: Posh youngster tucking into eggs and roll

indicators.note: tucking into means the young man goes inside the word for eggs

parts.note: roe is fish eggs
U means upper-class, posh
a lad is a young boy

explanation.surface: A posh boy eating eggs and a bread roll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking into' looks like eating but means going inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish rolled up around a filling, such as meat or sponge, is a roll.

clue.text: Devious work plans, as in this person's observations

indicators.note: devious means winding and indirect, so these letters take a twisted route

explanation.surface: Crooked plans for work, seen in a person's comments.
explanation.walkthrough: C. Northcote Parkinson observed that work expands to fill the time available; 'this person' is him, named by the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous maxim stated by the historian Parkinson, an observation about bureaucracy and work.

clue.text: Relaxing interval, but not for the cast?

definitions.text: Relaxing interval, but not for the cast?

parts.words: Relaxing interval, but not for the cast?
parts.note: a school break for games, but actors in a drama are working while their show is on

explanation.surface: An interval meant for relaxing is no rest for the actors on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, the answer is the duration of a theatrical performance, when the cast are hard at work.
explanation.definitionFit: A school break when children go out to have fun is a relaxing interval.

clue.text: Operational legacy: a connection problem

definitions.meaning: what remains after a surgical operation is the fibrous healing material left behind
such fibrous adhesions can wrongly join organs together, a medical problem of connection

explanation.surface: Sounds like a technical fault inherited from an operation, perhaps a dodgy network link.
explanation.definitionFit: Fibrous healing material is left after surgery and can form adhesions binding internal organs together.

clue.text: Pancake with cordial shunned by sailor

indicators.note: shunned by says the sailor's letters are taken out of the cordial word

parts.note: cordial means friendly, affable
AB, able seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor refuses a pancake served with a fruit cordial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cordial' looks like the drink but is the adjective; 'shunned by' removes AB from AFFABLE, leaving AFFLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A batter cake cooked in a gridded iron, close kin to a pancake.

clue.text: A winter resort, first centre for ski jumpers?

indicators.note: first says this letter is placed before the rest
centre for picks the middle letter of the word ski
resort read as re-sort means the letters are sorted again into a new order

explanation.surface: A winter resort with a centre for ski jumpers, the athletes who fly off ramps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday destination but means sort again; 'jumpers' are not athletes but sweaters.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumpers are knitted sweaters, an example of woollen garments; the question mark flags the definition by example.

clue.text: See 2
Comes off acid to achieve renewal

parts.note: to kick a habit is to come off it
tart means sour, acid

explanation.surface: Coming off drugs to start afresh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'acid' looks like the drug LSD but means sharp-tasting.
explanation.definitionFit: A boost that gets something going again, such as an economy, is a renewal.

clue.text: See 9
Kept together, getting on after rugby players

indicators.note: after says the old-age word follows the rugby word

parts.note: the forwards in rugby are called the pack
getting on means growing old

explanation.surface: Elderly members of a rugby team stick together.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods bundled and wrapped up as a unit are kept together for sale.

clue.text: Designer transport blocked by new resistance

indicators.note: blocked by means the new letter goes into the vehicle

parts.note: a plane is a form of transport
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: A designer's transport scheme is blocked by new opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: One who plans a building or town is its designer.

clue.text: Board/boards that Bill needs for passage

parts.note: a board of directors is a governing committee
to tread the boards is to act on the stage

explanation.surface: A company board wants a bill passed through approval.
explanation.walkthrough: A Bill in the UK Parliament goes through several readings, and in one phase a group of MPs scrutinises it line by line.
explanation.definitionFit: A parliamentary Bill must clear this detailed scrutiny phase on its way to becoming law.

clue.text: Place cross beside first motorway locations

indicators.note: beside means the motorway sits next to the rest

parts.note: the M1 was Britain's first motorway
lieu means place, as in in lieu of
X is a cross

explanation.surface: Instructions to set a cross beside the first motorway on a map.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1, Britain's first motorway, runs from London to Leeds; read as MI.
explanation.definitionFit: Surroundings or social settings, plural, are locations.

clue.text: Plain setter's got up to make an impression

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: the setter speaks of themself as I, so I've is setter's got
a dent is an impression made in a surface

explanation.surface: The plain setter has got up to make an impression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' looks like simple or a field but is an adjective meaning clear.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain as in clear to see; obvious.

clue.text: Easy-going daughter abandons prohibition for good

indicators.note: abandons means the daughter letter is given up and replaced

parts.note: a denial is a refusal or prohibition

explanation.surface: A relaxed daughter gives up prohibition for good.
explanation.definitionFit: Friendly and relaxed in manner, affable.

clue.text: Makes stricter rule — is poultry farmer coming round?

indicators.note: coming round means the farmer's words wrap about the rule letter

parts.note: a poultry farmer is one who has hens

explanation.surface: Does a poultry farmer coming round to the idea make the rules tougher?
explanation.walkthrough: 'is poultry farmer' becomes HAS HENS, and R sits between the A and S.
explanation.definitionFit: To toughen or make more severe is to make stricter.

clue.text: Girl's stay cut by a couple of seconds

indicators.note: cut by means the letters of the next pieces split the word for stay

parts.note: to lie somewhere is to stay or remain there
S is the abbreviation for second, so two of them make SS

explanation.surface: A girl's visit is cut short by a couple of seconds.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish and northern English word for a young woman or girl.

clue.text: See 17
Void in which valiant die horribly

indicators.note: horribly suggests the letters of valiant die are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: An empty space in which brave fighters perish gruesomely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Void' looks like a noun for an empty space but is a verb meaning cancel.
explanation.definitionFit: To void a contract or result is to cancel it, annul it legally.

clue.text: See 16
Upset wild plant

definitions.meaning: to upset someone is to fluster or unnerve them
yellow ... is a wildflower of meadows whose seeds clatter in their pods

explanation.surface: A wild plant that has been disturbed.
explanation.definitionFit: Unnerving someone is to fluster them; separately, a meadow wildflower bears this name for its noisy seed pods.

clue.text: Sweep interior of next outdoor shelter

indicators.note: interior of means the inside letters of the word next, dropping its ends

parts.note: a tent is a shelter used outdoors

explanation.surface: Sweeping out the inside of the tent next door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweep' looks like a broom action but is a noun for range.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweep of something is its range or scope, the area it covers.
